subject: PulsePay pilot: token economics, batching/caching boundaries & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Peter Liu <peter@pulsepay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: PulsePay pilot: token economics, batching/caching boundaries & next steps

Hi Peter —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Summary of the ask / pain points
- High per-interaction cost on current LLM provider; variable latencies during peak billing windows
- Need predictable monthly spend for merchant fraud-detection scoring (hard budget from finance)
- Willing to trade modest latency for 2x–4x cost reduction if accuracy stays within current thresholds

What we discussed (technical knobs)
- Token economics: expected tokens per request (~350 tokens/request baseline)
- Batching: potential 5–15% latency impact for requests that can be batched; 2–3x cost savings at 8–16 request batch sizes depending on arrival distribution
- KV prefix caching for repeated context (checkout templates) — could reduce token consumption by ~20%
- Quantized model variants for lower-cost inference with <1% quality delta (we'll validate with eval set)

Budget boundary and timeline
- PulsePay target: hard cap of $45k/month for pilot (including model compute + service margin)
- 90-day pilot preferred; goal to prove 2:1+ unit-economics improvement vs current vendor

Attachments: I've attached a short pilot scope and a redline MSA stub for procurement to review.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Confirm pilot budget boundary and primary success metric (accuracy/latency/cost) — action: Peter by Fri 7/30
2) Share small eval set (50–200 representative requests) for accuracy/quality validation — action: PulsePay
3) Internal cost ballpark + technical deep-dive scheduling — I can have a preliminary econ sketch by EOD Thu 7/29

If that all sounds right I’ll loop in Rishi (inference optimization) and Karthik (solutions engineering) and schedule a technical deep-dive.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0138

Subject: Re: PulsePay pilot: token economics, batching/caching boundaries & next steps

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear recap.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: procurement has approved up to $45k/month for a 90-day pilot; procurement will need a redlined MSA and a rough monthly spend profile before we can start billing commitments.
- Success metric: prefer a blended KPI — revenue-at-risk reduction (primary) + cost-per-inference reduction (secondary). We’ll quantify revenue-at-risk via our ops team and share a short mapping doc.
- Eval set: we can provide 150 anonymized examples by EOD Fri (I’ll coordinate with ops).

Two constraints to flag:
1) Peak-hour SLA: we need 95th percentile latency under 450ms for production-like traffic spikes; pilot can tolerate up to 600ms during batching windows
2) Data retention: anything stored for KV caching must be deletable on request and we need an explicit retention window for the pilot

Please include those items in the scope doc and loop in your security contact for the retention policy.

—Peter

Hi Peter — quick econ ballpark as promised (conservative):

Assumptions
- Baseline tokens/request: 350
- Hosted model unit compute: $0.00035 per token (baseline), quantized variant ~40% lower
- Batching efficiency: 2.5x cost reduction at avg batch size 10 (arrival permitting)
- KV cache reduction: 20% token savings for repeat context

Scenario A — no batching
- Effective unit cost ≈ $0.00028 per token (after minor caching/quantization)
- Per-request cost ≈ 350 * 0.00028 = $0.098 / request
- Monthly cost @ 1M requests ≈ $98k (exceeds your $45k cap)

Scenario B — batching + caching
- Effective unit cost ≈ $0.00011 per token
- Per-request cost ≈ 350 * 0.00011 = $0.0385 / request
- Monthly cost @ 1M requests ≈ $38.5k (within $45k cap with margin)

Interpretation
- With conservative arrival distribution, batching + KV caching gets you under target; without batching you will exceed the pilot cap.
- Next step: get the 150-request eval set and a sample traffic arrival curve (15-minute bins) so we can model achievable batching.

I’ll prepare a short one-pager with the two scenarios and recommended rollout (canary with 10% traffic, validate latency/quality, then expand).

Cheers,
Rishi
